clue.text: Back street in which one needs to inquire for jobs

indicators.note: in which says the second piece sits inside the turned-round first
back tells us to read the street abbreviation from right to left

parts.note: to inquire is to ask

explanation.surface: Someone wandering a back street asking around for work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back street' reads as an alley, but 'Back' is the reversal signal and 'in which' the container; 'one needs to' is just link padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks and jobs are plain synonyms for pieces of work to be done.

clue.text: What people call us in explosive competition

indicators.note: in places the phrase about our name inside the explosive

parts.note: TNT is the explosive trinitrotoluene
what people call us is our name

explanation.surface: A volatile contest where the team's reputation is at stake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What people call us' is a whole phrase giving two words; 'in' makes the explosive wrap around them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament is a series of contests between many competitors for an overall prize.

clue.text: Siberian place of punishment could produce ailments

indicators.note: could produce suggests the letters can be reworked to make something new

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Harsh exile in Siberia that might bring on illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could produce' rearranges AILMENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners exiled to Siberia under the tsars were often forced to labour in mines extracting salt.

clue.text: Dons went wild — expelled from the university

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters are running out of control, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: University lecturers lost their temper and threw a student out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges DONS WENT. 'Dons' points at university teachers, which suits the surface neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: In British universities, a student expelled for misconduct is said to be sent down, especially at Oxford and Cambridge.

clue.text: Love in romance novel somewhere in Africa

indicators.note: in places the zero for love inside the rearranged letters
novel as an adjective means new, so the letters of romance are made new by rearranging

parts.note: taken as written
love is nil in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A love story in a romantic novel set somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges ROMANCE into CAMERON, and 'in' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cameroon is a country in west-central Africa, so it is one example of a place on that continent.

clue.text: Model given a part on stage

definitions.meaning: to model a figure is to shape it, as with metal poured into a mould
an actor chosen for a role has been assigned it

explanation.surface: A model handed an acting role.
explanation.definitionFit: Casting both shapes molten metal in a mould and assigns actors their roles in a production.

clue.text: Provides some point with jokes

parts.note: E, for east, is one of the compass points
quips are witty jokes

explanation.surface: Someone who livens up a talk with gags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass point here, not the point of a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip someone is to furnish or supply them with what they need.

clue.text: Busy tenant

definitions.meaning: used as a verb, to busy oneself is to keep oneself engaged
used as a verb, to tenant a house is to live in it as a resident

explanation.surface: A tenant with plenty to do.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like an adjective and noun but act as verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To occupy means both to keep someone engaged and to live in a property.

clue.text: Either way, it's high time

indicators.note: either way says the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A remark that, however you look at it, something is overdue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high time' sounds like overdue but means the middle of the day, the sun at its height, as in the western High Noon.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is when the sun stands highest, so twelve o'clock is the high point of the day.

clue.text: A most unfair condition

parts.note: fair can mean good-looking, so the most unfair state is being the least attractive, not the most unjust

explanation.surface: A complaint about a deeply unjust situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfair' reads as unjust, but here it means not fair in the sense of not beautiful.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ugliest means least fair-looking, so plainness of appearance is the state described.

clue.text: After bad act I become silent

indicators.note: after says the word for become follows the jumbled letters
bad suggests the letters of act I have gone wrong and are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
to turn can mean to become, as milk turns sour

explanation.surface: An actor who gave a bad performance and then fell silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges ACT I into TACI.
explanation.definitionFit: Taciturn describes someone who says very little, reserved and uncommunicative in speech.

clue.text: He provides all his workers with a home

definitions.text: He provides all his workers with a home

parts.words: He provides all his workers with a home
parts.note: the workers are worker bees, and their home is a hive kept by a beekeeper

explanation.surface: A generous employer who houses all his staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workers' suggests employees, but worker bees are meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A beekeeper looks after colonies of bees, housing them in hives he maintains.

clue.text: Large number coming in drunk in coma, wandering around

indicators.note: coming in tells us the large number enters the scrambled letters
drunk suggests the letters of in coma are reeling and out of order

parts.note: taken as written
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, a large number

explanation.surface: Someone so drunk they are almost in a coma, staggering about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges IN COMA into NOMAIC, and 'coming in' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic peoples roam from place to place without a fixed home, so they are always on the move.

clue.text: Issue needing to be raised

definitions.meaning: issue means offspring, a person's descendants
young ones must be brought up by parents

explanation.surface: A matter that ought to be brought up at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' and 'raised' suggest a topic for discussion, but issue is offspring and raised means brought up.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a legal and formal word for offspring, and young offspring are what parents rear.

clue.text: Top design created by husband bearing pen used by the French

parts.note: a person's bearing is their air or manner
a pen is an enclosure for animals, such as a sty for pigs
le is the French word for the

explanation.surface: A design, perhaps a pen, created by a husband for French use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like a writing tool but is a pig's enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: The top here is the head, so a design for it is the way someone's hair is cut and arranged.

clue.text: Seer who may be called to account?

definitions.text: Seer who may be called to account?

parts.words: Seer who may be called to account?
parts.note: a seer is literally one who sees, and the account is testimony in court

explanation.surface: A prophet who might be made to answer for his predictions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seer' suggests a prophet, but it means someone who saw an event and may be summoned to give an account in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who watched a crime may be summoned to court to describe what they saw.

clue.text: Perpetual figure that causes matrimonial disputes

definitions.text: Perpetual figure that causes matrimonial disputes

parts.note: perpetual means lasting for ever, endless
a triangle is a geometric figure with three sides

explanation.surface: A never-ending shape blamed for marital rows.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the familiar phrase describes a love affair between three people.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a relationship of two lovers and a spouse, a classic cause of strife within a marriage.

clue.text: Correct bill going to cleric

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill to be paid
a curate is an assistant member of the clergy

explanation.surface: A proper invoice being sent to a vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correct' looks like a verb but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate and correct both mean free from error, precise in every detail.

clue.text: Stick with revised point showing common sense

parts.note: to stick things together is to gum them

indicators.note: revised suggests the letters of point have been reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Holding to an amended argument as the sensible course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges POINT into PTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Gumption is shrewd practical intelligence, the resourcefulness to act sensibly.

clue.text: Reference book shows Zodiac sign he's within

indicators.note: within says the second piece is placed inside the zodiac sign

parts.note: Taurus the bull is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A book of astrology revealing that someone was born under a particular star sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' is the container signal; the apostrophe in "he's" is ignored, as crosswords usually do with punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a book listing synonyms, consulted rather than read through, hence a work of reference.

clue.text: Got paid employment, with organ study set up

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the word for study is raised, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a den is a small private room for study

explanation.surface: A worker on a salary, with medical study ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns DEN into NED.
explanation.definitionFit: Earned means gained money in return for work, receiving wages for a job done.

clue.text: Build up a hundred to go on new cure

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for one hundred

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of cure are given a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A batsman building a century on the way to recovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CURE into CRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Accrue means to accumulate or grow over time, as interest gathers in an account.

clue.text: President returning note that's instrumental in showing boastfulness

parts.note: Trump is a US president

indicators.note: returning tells us the musical note comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A president coming back to a note that helped make him look boastful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns TE into ET. The definition plays on the brass instrument and on blowing one's own horn as boasting.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow one's own horn means to brag, and the brass instrument gives its name to that kind of loud self-praise.

clue.text: Continentals involved in fracas

indicators.note: involved can mean tangled up, so the letters are jumbled together

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Visitors from the Continent caught up in a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continentals' suggests mainland Europeans, but here it means people of the African continent.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Africa are natives of a continent, so they are continentals in a literal sense.

clue.text: A long way off from the safari centre

indicators.note: centre says keep the middle letters of safari, dropping each end

explanation.surface: A trip far from the heart of a safari.
explanation.walkthrough: The central four letters of sAFARi.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means at or to a great distance, far away.

clue.text: Pore over books endlessly as boss

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter of the word for poring over books is dropped

parts.note: to pore over books is to study

explanation.surface: A boss who studies without ever stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' looks like a manager but means a raised knob or stud.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a round raised ornament on a surface, like a decorative nail head.

clue.text: Doctor is initially eager to give discourse

parts.note: to doctor a patient is to treat them

indicators.note: initially says take only the opening letter of eager

explanation.surface: A keen doctor ready to give a lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun but is the verb to treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal written discourse examining a subject at length.

clue.text: Once more judged and freed from blame

parts.note: re is a prefix meaning again, once more
to deem is to judge or consider

explanation.surface: Someone judged a second time and cleared.
explanation.definitionFit: Being redeemed means being saved or delivered from sin or blame, cleared of fault.

clue.text: Birds in wilderness

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the word wilderness

explanation.surface: Birds living out in the wild.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run inside wildERNESs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernes are sea eagles, a type of large bird familiar from crosswords.
